parts.instructions: Answer these questions about your daily life and free time activities.
questions: Do you work or are you a student?
What do you do in your free time?
Have you ever joined any clubs or groups?
How do you usually spend your weekends?
Do you prefer spending time alone or with others? Why?

cueCard.topic: Describe a club or group you would like to join.
bullets: what club or group it is
how you found out about it
and explain why you would like to join this club or group

questions: Why do you think people join clubs and associations?
What are the benefits of being part of a community group?
Do you think young people today are less likely to join clubs than previous generations?
How can universities encourage students to participate in extracurricular activities?
Some clubs charge membership fees. Do you think this is fair? Why or why not?
What role do social activities play in helping people adapt to new environments?

_legacyTask.title: University Clubs and Associations
_legacyTask.format: Cambridge IELTS 1 (1996) — Part 3 Elicitation: candidate asks examiner questions
_legacyTask.scenario: You have just arrived at a new university. It is orientation week and you want to know about the different clubs and associations you can join.
_legacyTask.role: Your examiner is a Student Union representative.

interviewerNotes.description: The interviewer has information about three clubs to share when asked.

prompts.details: Meets once a week in Student Centre, near Library. All welcome. Helps you to meet other students. Financial contributions welcome.
Meets once a week in Library. Not suitable for beginners. Plays other universities. Serious players only. No subscription.
Meets every day at lunch-time in student area near canteen. All welcome. Arranges tournaments. $5.00 subscription.

parts.instructions: Answer these questions about your studies and education experience.
questions: What subject are you studying? Why did you choose it?
How do you usually manage your time when you have assignments due?
Have you ever had difficulty completing an assignment on time?
What resources do you use when you need help with your studies?
Do you prefer working on assignments alone or in a group?

cueCard.topic: Describe a time when you had to ask for help with your studies or work.
bullets: and explain how you felt about asking for help

questions: Why do some students struggle to meet assignment deadlines?
What support services should universities provide for students who are falling behind?
Do you think strict deadlines help or harm the learning process?
How has technology changed the way students access information for their studies?
Some people say that asking for help is a sign of weakness. What is your view?
What can employers do to support employees who are studying while working?

_legacyTask.title: Asking for an Extension
_legacyTask.format: Cambridge IELTS 1 (1996) — Part 3 Elicitation: candidate asks examiner questions
_legacyTask.scenario: You have to give in a piece of work to your lecturer next Wednesday. You need two more weeks to prepare the assignment because you have had difficulty obtaining the reference books.
_legacyTask.role: Your examiner is your lecturer. Find out if you can have an extension.
topicsToAsk: assistance with writing for overseas students

interviewerNotes.description: The student is seeking extra time for an assignment. After some resistance, agree to an extension of one week.
prompts: The student may need to write a letter.
The student has had plenty of time to prepare the work and should not really need two more weeks.
Provide some idea about where he/she may get hold of the books.
Offer advice about the 'Learning Assistance Centre' on the campus which helps students with essay writing.

parts.instructions: Answer these questions about holidays and celebrations.
questions: What is your favourite public holiday? Why?
How do people in your country typically celebrate national holidays?
Do you prefer spending holidays with family or travelling?
Are there any holidays or festivals you don't enjoy? Why not?
How do public holidays in your country compare with those in other countries?

cueCard.topic: Describe a public holiday or festival that is important in your country.
bullets: what the holiday or festival is
and explain why this holiday or festival is important to your culture

questions: Why are public holidays important for a country's cultural identity?
How do public holidays affect the economy — are they good or bad for business?
Do you think there should be more or fewer public holidays? Why?
What can visitors learn about a country by experiencing its holidays?
Some traditional holidays are losing popularity among young people. Why do you think this happens?
How can governments balance preserving traditions with modern lifestyles?

_legacyTask.title: The Public Holiday
_legacyTask.format: Cambridge IELTS 1 (1996) — Part 3 Elicitation: candidate asks examiner questions
_legacyTask.scenario: There will soon be a public holiday in the country your examiner comes from. You want to find out about the holiday.
_legacyTask.role: Your examiner comes from a country with a public holiday.
topicsToAsk: how she/he plans to spend the day

interviewerNotes.description: Choose a lesser known public holiday from your country. Be prepared to provide accurate information on the history and significance of the day.
prompts: If in-country, tell the candidate how you will spend the day.
If in a non-English speaking country, tell the candidate how people normally spend this day back home.
Provide information about the availability of shops, services and banks on the day.

parts.instructions: Answer these questions about travel and tourism.
questions: Do you enjoy travelling? Why or why not?
What kind of places do you like to visit when you travel?
Have you ever been on a group excursion or tour? How was it?
What do you think is the best way to explore a new place?
Do you prefer planning trips in advance or being spontaneous?

cueCard.topic: Describe an excursion or day trip that you have been on or would like to go on.
bullets: where you went or would like to go
who you went with or would go with
what you did or would do there
and explain why this excursion was or would be memorable

questions: What are the benefits of organised excursions compared to independent travel?
How has tourism changed the way local communities live?
What should travellers consider when choosing what to wear or bring on a trip?
Do you think travel is too expensive for most people? What can be done about it?
Some tourist destinations are becoming overcrowded. How should this problem be addressed?
What role does food play in the travel experience?

_legacyTask.title: The Excursion
_legacyTask.format: Cambridge IELTS 1 (1996) — Part 3 Elicitation: candidate asks examiner questions
_legacyTask.scenario: The Overseas Students' Club is organising an excursion to a local tourist spot. You are thinking of joining the excursion.
_legacyTask.role: Your examiner is one of the organisers.

interviewerNotes.description: Select an authentic tourist destination about two hours' drive from your city. Provide information according to local facts.
prompts: Details about what can be seen/done there.
Meals not provided — students can buy or bring food.

_validation.note: Cambridge IELTS 1 (1996) uses the old 5-part speaking format. The 4 original Part 3 Elicitation tasks (candidate asks examiner questions) are preserved in _legacyTask. Modern 3-part format tasks (Part 1 Interview, Part 2 Long Turn, Part 3 Discussion) were generated by Claude based on the themes of the original tasks. All modern content is aligned with current IELTS Speaking test format.
